name: Knight of the Glen

attributes.attribute: also called O'Donohue of the Glen
the fairy king of the upper lake of Killarney
cast a spell so a log bore John's shape
frightened his kin on his return home

sources: Curtin, Jeremiah. *Hero-Tales of Ireland.* New York: Benjamin Blom, 1894, 17.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Knight of the Glen is a figure of Irish folklore. He is also called O'Donohue of the Glen. In the stories he is Daniel O'Donohue, a fairy ruler of the northern waters of Killarney's lake in Munster. One tale says he swept away a local fellow, John Connors. He cast a spell on a log so the wood wore the man's shape. He kept the true John asleep in the Otherworld. The wooden stand-in was laid out and buried with full ceremony. The genuine John kept on sleeping in Fairy. When he woke at last and came home, his family and friends fled in fright. They could hardly believe he was not a ghost.

okr.objective: The Knight of the Glen is the fairy king who lets only a log wear a man's shape.
key_results: He ruled the upper lake of Killarney.
